st.headline: Singapore’s retail sales growth rose 0.7% in August
st.teaser: Retail sales excluding motor vehicles, parts and accessories rose 1.6% year on year.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Singapore’s retail sales growth expanded 0.7% year on year in August 2026, following the 1.3% growth in July, according to data from the Singapore Department of Statistics (SingStat).
In a release on Oct 5, SingStat said retail sales excluding motor vehicles, parts and accessories rose 1.6% year on year, compared with 1.3% growth in July.
On a month-on-month and seasonally adjusted basis, retail sales fell 1% in August. Excluding motor vehicles, parts and accessories, sales rose 0.6%.
Total retail sales were estimated at $4.5 billion in August, with online transactions accounting for 15.7 % of the total, up from 15.2% in July.
Within the retail trade sector, the majority of industries recorded year-on-year growth in sales in August.
Cosmetics, toiletries and medical goods saw the strongest year-on-year growth, with sales going up by 11.2%, partly driven by higher sales of cosmetics and toiletries.

This is closely followed by the computer and telecommunications equipment industry, which grew by 10.7%, driven by more sales of mobile phones. Other industries that recorded year-on-year increases include recreational goods, which rose 4.3% and petrol service stations, which rose 3.2%. In contrast, motor vehicles, parts and accessories recorded year-on-year declines in sales of 4.6%, while retailers of watches and jewellery saw a dip in sales of 2.7% in August. The SingStat data also showed that food and beverage services sales fell by 1.6% year on year in August, extending July’s 1.9% decline.
The total F&B sales were estimated at $1.7 billion, with online transactions accounting for 20.6% of the total, down from 20.9% in July.

Within the F&B services sector, cafes saw the biggest drop in year-on-year sales of 5.3%, while foodcourts and other eating places recorded year-on-year sales fall of 4.8% in August. Restaurants’ sales also decreased by 2.1%.
In contrast, sales at fast-food outlets rose by 7.8%, while those of food caterers increased by 2.9%.

cna.headline: Mediacorp 987 launches radio-themed escape room experience at Xcape Singapore
cna.teaser: The experience will feature seven 987 personalities through audio and visual elements and will run from now until Nov 1.
fullText: Mediacorp 987 has teamed up with Xcape Singapore for a new escape room experience that puts players inside a fictionalised version of the radio station, where they must solve puzzles and uncover the mystery behind a hijacked radio signal.
Mediacorp 987's Signal Hijacked: The Purge Protocol runs from now until Nov 1, 2026, and is billed as Singapore's first radio-themed escape room experience.

Players take on the roles of new interns arriving at 987 for their first day. A guided tour of the station by a 987 radio personality takes a darker turn at night when a citywide Purge begins, and participants will need to solve the mystery event before time runs out.
The 75-minute experience is designed for groups of three to eight people.
Seven 987 personalities – Ann Nicole, Avery Aloysius, Germaine Tan, Joakim Gomez, Louisa Kan, Natasha Faisal and Sonia Chew – feature in the experience through curated audio and visual elements.
Tickets are priced at S$39.90 per person for standard sessions and S$45.90 per person for peak sessions after 6pm.
The experience runs at Xcape Singapore from now until Nov 1. Tickets are available through Xcape Singapore's website .

listening.title: Singapore's Hawker Centres Embrace Digital Payments
listening.transcript: As Singapore marches towards its Smart Nation vision, more than ninety percent of hawker stalls now accept SGQR e-payments. This digital shift has reduced the hassle of handling physical cash and coins during busy lunch hours. While older patrons initially found the transition challenging, community digital ambassadors have successfully bridged the gap. Now, grabbing a bowl of laksa is as simple as a quick scan of your mobile phone.

economistArticle.title: The Coming Deluge: How the LNG Crunch Will Give Way to a Massive Glut
paras: The global energy market has spent the past few years on a knife-edge. Following the geopolitical disruptions of 2022, when Europe scrambled to replace Russian pipeline gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG) became the world’s ultimate economic security blanket. Prices skyrocketed, leaving poorer nations in Asia in the dark while wealthier economies locked down every spare drop of super-chilled fuel. This acute supply crunch triggered a frantic, capital-intensive race to build massive new export terminals, particularly along the US Gulf Coast and in Qatar.

Yet, the multi-billion-dollar investments designed to cure today's deficit are poised to overshoot demand. Energy analysts predict that between 2025 and 2028, a staggering wave of new liquefaction capacity will come online, expanding global supply by over forty percent. This impending supply surge threatens to transform a highly congested seller's market into a highly competitive buyer's paradise. The world, it seems, is pivoting rapidly from an almighty LNG crunch to an equally disruptive glut.

For major Asian importing hubs like Singapore, which has positioned itself as a critical trading node, this transition brings both relief and complexity. Cheaper and more abundant gas will lower electricity generation costs and stabilize industrial operations across the region. However, a sudden collapse in prices could derail investments in cleaner alternatives. If cheap fossil gas remains plentiful, local utilities might find themselves less incentivised to aggressively pursue costlier solar power or hydrogen energy infrastructure.

Furthermore, the impending glut will challenge the business models of energy giants that locked themselves into expensive, long-term supply contracts during the height of the crunch. Portfolio players will have to navigate a market where spot prices could plunge below the cost of production. Flexibility in contracts, such as destination-free clauses and indexation shifts, will become paramount as buyers regain the upper hand.

Ultimately, the cyclical nature of commodity markets is playing out in textbook fashion. The high prices that punished consumers over the last three years have successfully stimulated the investment needed to secure future supply. But in their rush to avoid energy insecurity, producers may have overcompensated, paving the way for a protracted period of oversupply that will reshape the global energy map for the next decade.
economistArticle.cn:
全球能源市场在过去几年中一直处于千钧一发的紧要关头。继2022年地缘政治动荡、欧洲争相取代俄罗斯管道天然气之后，液化天然气（LNG）成为了全球终极的经济安全保障。价格一路飙升，导致亚洲较贫困的国家陷入黑暗，而较富裕的经济体则锁定了每一滴多余的超冷燃料。这种急剧的供应紧张引发了一场疯狂的、资本密集型的竞赛，旨在建设庞大的新出口终端，特别是在美国墨西哥湾沿岸和卡塔尔。

然而，旨在解决当前赤字的数百亿美元投资注定会超出需求。能源分析师预测，在2025年至2028年之间，惊人的新液化产能将陆续投产，使全球供应量扩大40%以上。这一即将到来的供应激增恐将使一个高度拥挤的卖方市场转变为极具竞争力的买方天堂。世界似乎正在迅速从全能型的LNG紧缺转向同样具有颠覆性的供应过剩。

对于像新加坡这样已将自己定位为关键贸易节点的亚洲主要进口枢纽而言，这一转变既带来了缓解，也带来了复杂性。更便宜、更充足的天然气将降低发电成本，并稳定该地区的工业运营。然而，价格的突然崩盘可能会阻碍对更清洁替代能源的投资。如果廉价的化石天然气依然充足，当地公用事业公司可能会发现自己缺乏积极追求成本更高的太阳能或氢能基础设施的动力。

此外，即将到来的供应过剩将挑战能源巨头的商业模式，这些巨头在供应紧张的高峰期锁定了昂贵的长期供应合同。组合型交易商将不得不应对现货价格可能跌破生产成本的市场。随着买家重新夺回主动权，合同的灵活性（如无目的地条款和指数挂钩转变）将变得至关重要。

归根结底，大宗商品市场的周期性特征正在以教科书般的方式上演。过去三年惩罚消费者的昂贵价格，已成功刺激了确保未来供应所需的投资。但在避免能源不安全感的匆忙中，生产商可能过度补偿，从而为可能重塑未来十年全球能源版图的长期供应过剩铺平了道路。
